chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Ibn from Ibn Muskhan from Al-Halabi said:

I asked him about the prayer in the month of Ramadan, so he said: 'Thirteen rak'at, including the Witr, and two rak'at of the morning prayer after Fajr. Thus did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) pray, and I pray thus. And if it were better, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would not have left it.'
And from him from Hammad from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

I asked him about the prayer in the month of Ramadan, he said: 'Thirteen rak'at, including the Witr, and two rak'at before the Fajr prayer. Thus did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) pray, and if it were a virtue, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would have acted upon it and been more deserving.'

key_terms.أَعْمَلَ بِهِ: To act upon it (as a practice)
key_terms.رَكْعَتَا اَلصُّبْحِ: The two rak'at of the Fajr prayer

ai.seo_question: How many rak'at are performed in the night prayers of Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the standard practice of thirteen rak'at for Ramadan night prayers (Qiyam), including Witr, a view strongly supported by the consensus of Shia jurists. The narration highlights the continuity of practice between the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), using the Prophet's adherence to this specific number as definitive proof of its virtue and authenticity. It underscores the Shia emphasis on following the Ahl al-Bayt's interpretation of prophetic tradition in ritual worship.
